title: The declaration table requires a specId no reader enforces
scopeProof: The docs table is the normative declaration contract a reader follows; no code path validates it.
claim: The docs require a specId in a sub-track description.json that no reader validates and that is semically a numeric prefix elsewhere.

title: The track/sub-track example writes children_ids without the parent prefix
scopeProof: expectedChildrenIds prepends the identity; compareTrackChildren treats a bare entry as foreign.
claim: The example's children_ids entries omit the track prefix that every writer and test uses.

title: The implementation summary says a deeper layout is reported but no reader scans a folder inside a sub-track
scopeProof: The statement is in the packet's own Known Limitations, so it is the contract a reader relies on.
claim: The known-limitation row says a deeper layout is reported, but no reader scans folders inside a sub-track.

title: The packet completion percentage contradicts its complete status
scopeProof: The three fields are in the same packet and name the same transaction.
claim: completion_pct is 90 while the spec, acceptance closure and recent_action all describe the packet as complete.

title: The sub-track container parent_id contract has two writers with different answers
scopeProof: Both writers target the same parent_id field of the same folder, and the docs name the value.
claim: The docs and repair-derived say a sub-track parent_id is its track, while resolveParentId returns null for the container.
